[LNLS.3.3c] **A multi-pattern rule needs an anchor at all.** A
multi-pattern rule carrying no cross-pattern equality constraint is a
compile error: with nothing pinning the two sides together the join
degenerates to a scan, which is the whole condition `linear_scan: false`
exists to exclude.

An equality constraint is an `==` between a slot read of each side, as
[LNLS.3.3] writes it. An `==` between any other expressions, such as two
non-base assertions ([RLOW.6.1.10]), pins nothing, and a rule whose only
cross-pattern equalities are such is this clause's refusal.
